e-3631.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With Sine or Cosine Trigonometric Functions
e-3631.problem: Find the derivative of $y =  3\cos x  + 4\sin x + 2x^3.$
e-3631.worked_solution:
We know that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} ( \sin x ) = \cos x,$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} ( \cos x ) = -\sin x.$ Applying these formulas, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3cos⁡x+4sin⁡x+2{x}^{3}) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(cos⁡x)+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sin⁡x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}) \\  & =-3sin⁡x+4cos⁡x+2(3){x}^{2} \\  & =-3sin⁡x+4cos⁡x+6{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-3632.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With the Tangent Trigonometric Function
e-3632.problem: Find the slope of $y = 4\tan x + 5x$ at $x = 0.$
e-3632.worked_solution:
The slope at $x=0$ is given by the value of the derivative $y'$ at $x=0.$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (\tan x) = \sec^2 x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4tan⁡x+5x) \\  & =4{sec}^{2}⁡x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & =4{sec}^{2}⁡0+5 \\  & =4\cdot 1+5 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope is $9.$

Find the derivative of y=−2cos⁡x+x−2.

a
−2sin⁡x−2x−3

−2sin⁡x−2x−2

We know that ddx(cos⁡x)=−sin⁡x. Applying this formula, we have

dydx=ddx(−2cos⁡x+x−2)=−2(−sin⁡x)+(−2)x−2−1=2sin⁡x−2x−3.

$$

after.problem: What is the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=2x-5cos⁡x$ at the point $x=\frac{\pi }{6}?$
after.worked_solution:
The slope at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ is given by the value of the derivative ${y}^{′}$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(cos⁡x)=-sin⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-5cos⁡x) \\  & =2-5(-sin⁡x) \\  & =2+5sin⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(30) & =2+5sin⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =2+5(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =2+\frac{5}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate of change is $\frac{9}{2}.$

after.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6({x}^{2}-cos⁡x)+5) \\  & =6\cdot 2x+6sin⁡x+0 \\  & =12x+6sin⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Calculate the instantaneous rate of change of the function $f(x)=-tan⁡x$ when $x=\pi .$
after.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change  when $x=\pi $ is given by the value of the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ at $x=\pi .$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-tan⁡x) \\  & =-{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\pi ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-{sec}^{2}⁡\pi  \\  & =-1\cdot (-1)^{2} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate of change is $-1.$

Question 6
?

Calculate the instantaneous rate of change of the function f(x)=−tan⁡x when x=π.

a
1
b
−2
c
2
d
−1
e
13
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The instantaneous rate of change when x=π is given by the value of the derivative f′(x) at x=π.

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that ddx(tan⁡x)=sec2⁡x. We get

f′(x)=ddx(−tan⁡x)=−sec2⁡x.

Evaluating at x=π, we get

f′(π)=−sec2⁡π=−1⋅(−1)2=−1.

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change is −1.

content.problem: Calculate the instantaneous rate of change of the function $f(x)=-tan⁡x$ when $x=\pi .$
content.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change  when $x=\pi $ is given by the value of the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ at $x=\pi .$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-tan⁡x) \\  & =-{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\pi ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-{sec}^{2}⁡\pi  \\  & =-1\cdot (-1)^{2} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate of change is $-1.$

decision.explanation: Differentiate inside the parentheses and multiply by 3: y'=3(2x-2sec²x)+0=6x-6sec²x. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ Applying this formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3({x}^{2}-2tan⁡x)+4) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}-6tan⁡x+4) \\  & =3\cdot 2x-6{sec}^{2}⁡x+0 \\  & =6x-6{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Find y′ for y=3(x2−2tan⁡x)+4.

a
3−6sec2⁡x
b
6x−6sec2⁡x
c

d

y′=ddx(3(x2−2tan⁡x)+4)=ddx(3x2−6tan⁡x+4)=3⋅2x−6sec2⁡x+0=6x−6sec2⁡x.

$$
